title: Chapter 13
content:
Jakyeong slid the bedroom nightstand drawer open and tossed inside the luxury watch Seok-joo had handed him as a bribe.

Needing to rinse off the grime of the night, he stripped down and stepped into the shower. As icy water cascaded over his head, the memory of that tattoo flashed behind his eyelids.

On the day he saw his biological parents for the last time, a crew of men sporting that exact four-horned dokkaebi ink had kicked down their front door.

They had beaten the family of three half to death, blindfolded their swollen eyes, bound their limbs with zip-ties, and hauled them away into the night. They ended up in a pitch-black warehouse without a single window. On day one, his father was dragged out and never returned. On day two, his mother vanished into the dark.

And on the third night... the heavy steel door creaked open once more.

The man who stepped through the shadows was none other than Mr. Wang, their Chinese neighbor. Hoisting the battered, blood-soaked young Jakyeong over his shoulder, he had carried the boy out into the night air. Passing the exit, Jakyeong caught sight of two guards lying unconscious in a pool of blood. Beside them, sticking out from an open steel oil drum, was a limp human arm. Crimson polish coated the fingernails, and the cheap imitation-jeweled bracelet his mother wore every single day caught the faint moonlight.

Staring down at the water swirling down the drain, Jakyeong gritted his teeth against the rush of bitter nostalgia. It wasn't grief or vengeance fueling his anger. If those thugs hadn't murdered his parents that night, he probably would have slit their throats with his own two hands eventually.

His chest felt heavy, hollowed out. A cold beer sounded necessary.

Toweling off and pulling on fresh clothes, he stepped out into the lounge—only to freeze in his tracks. Sitting comfortably on the leather sofa was Kang Il-hyun.

Of course.

Giving up on the beer, Jakyeong walked over with quiet steps. Master of the house or not, the man had a knack for wandering in and out of private quarters like an intrusive phantom.

"Come sit down for a moment," Il-hyun said, gesturing to the seat opposite him.

Jakyeong sat, folding his hands politely in his lap.

"I owe you an apology for earlier," Il-hyun began, his tone measured. "I should have kept a tighter leash on Seok-joo. It was my oversight."

"Oh, please, don't worry about it," Jakyeong murmured, casting his eyes downward. "Thanks to your consideration, I really enjoyed the gallery exhibition."

"Is that so?"

Jakyeong wasn't going out of his way to defend Seok-joo. If Il-hyun decided to beat the little junkie to death tomorrow, it wouldn't cost Jakyeong a wink of sleep. But having pocketed a hundred-thousand-dollar watch, he couldn't completely burn the bridge either. A little damage control was the least he could do.

"It was great meeting guys my own age, too. We had fun."

"Hmm... that's rather unexpected."

"Pardon?"

"No matter how I look at it, that crowd hardly seems like the right company for someone of your background."

"No, really... they weren't bad at all," Jakyeong stammered softly. "They were very welcoming."

"I'm glad to hear that. But you understand, don't you?" Il-hyun leaned in slightly, his dark eyes fixing onto Jakyeong's face. "Hanging out is fine, but you mustn't cross any lines. If something happens to you, I'd have no face left to show your grandfather, who entrusted you to our care."

"Yes... I understand."

Il-hyun nodded with a satisfied smile. "Good. We'll leave today's events at that, then. I'll let you get some rest."

As Il-hyun rose to his feet, Jakyeong hesitated, then stood up quickly to stop him.

"Director Kang... may I ask a small favor?"

Il-hyun paused, turning back. "Go ahead."

"You mentioned you'd have the camera removed from my bedroom, but... it's still mounted up there."

"Ah. Is it causing you that much discomfort?"

"Well... yes," Jakyeong said, fidgeting with his hemline. "Being cooped up in the house all day is suffocating enough as it is, but having a lens watching me while I sleep makes it worse..."

The subtle temperature drop in Il-hyun's eyes made Jakyeong's stomach drop. Damn it. I shouldn't have said the house feels suffocating.

As Jakyeong scrambled to find a graceful way to backtrack, Il-hyun gave a slow, deliberate nod.

"Suffocating. So my house makes you feel trapped."

"N-No, that's not what I meant—"

"I thought the square footage was generous enough," Il-hyun mused aloud, a razor-thin smirk touching his lips. "Perhaps I should have built it bigger."

"No, really, it's not that—"

"My mistake entirely. I should've made it fucking colossal."

The sarcastic bite was delivered with a pleasant, model-ready smile that made Jakyeong want to grind his teeth to dust. Fucking psycho. God, I can't stand this guy.

Suppressing the urge to lunge across the table, Jakyeong decided to double down while the conversational door was still cracked open.

"To be completely honest, it does feel a bit confining..." Jakyeong mumbled, keeping his voice small and timid. "I feel like I'm being watched even when I'm in bed. And... I’ve always had a huge passion for interior design, so I wanted to explore the estate, but... every single door is locked tight..."

Il-hyun tilted his head, his dark eyes narrowing into a sharp, searching gaze.

Jakyeong didn't flinch. He met the stare head-on, widening his eyes into a picture of innocent, harmless curiosity.

"And where, exactly, were you so eager to explore?"

Screw it. In for a penny, in for a pound.

"The... basement, maybe?"

Il-hyun’s expression went completely still.

A cold prickle ran down Jakyeong's spine. Did I push too far? Did I blow it? Should I have just waited for Wang Han to finish synthesizing the biometric prints? A dozen tactical escape routes flashed through his mind before Il-hyun's face softened, letting out a slow, amused nod.

"You should have said so earlier. It's not like I have anything to hide from you."

Jakyeong bit the inside of his cheek, forcing his lips into a bright, surprised smile. Wait, seriously? So the housekeeper wasn't just blowing smoke when she said Il-hyun might show him around.

"Want to go take a look right now?" Il-hyun asked.

"I... I heard it was your private quarters... Would that really be alright?"

Now that you're offering, it's making me nervous.

Instead of answering, Il-hyun closed the distance between them with two long strides, stopping bare inches from Jakyeong's chest. Jakyeong instinctively started to lean back, but caught himself, looking up into those pitch-black pupils looking down at him.

"I have very little patience for people whose words contradict their actions," Il-hyun whispered softly.

"Pardon?"

"Your eyes are burning with curiosity, yet your mouth keeps playing polite. Why lie?"

"..."

"If you want to see it, I'll take you down right now."

Jakyeong’s brain scrambled to keep up with the sudden shift.

"Well? Do you want to go?"

"...Yes. Please show me."

The tight line of Il-hyun's mouth curved upward into an amused grin. "Follow me," he murmured, turning on his heel.

Left standing in his wake, Jakyeong let out a silent, ragged breath through his teeth. Getting access to the restricted zone this easily was a massive operational breakthrough—so why did an ominous, crawling dread keep wrapping around his ribs like a snake?

Staring blankly into his lukewarm cup of tea, Kang Tae-han slowly lifted his eyes.

Sitting across from him in the private booth was his stepmother, Kim Sun-young, lazily twisting the diamond ring on her fourth finger. Resting on the polished mahogany table between them was a single photograph she had slid over moments ago:

Jang Yi-an. The Hong Kong heir who had arrived in Seoul a few days back, currently staying at Kang Il-hyun’s residence and seen wandering the city with Kang Seok-joo earlier today.

Tae-han glanced around the venue. She had summoned him to a boutique lounge on the quiet outskirts of Seoul, completely clearing out the staff and patrons to ensure total privacy. The only other soul in the room was Director Yoon, her trusted confidant, standing guard by the door.

Pushing his wire-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose, Tae-han slid the photograph back across the table.

"I hear what you're saying, Mother. But unfortunately... I cannot fulfill your request."

Sun-young reached into her designer handbag, retrieving a slim cigarette and a gold lighter. People often said a woman’s hands and neck were the first to betray her age, but the rule didn't apply to her; her porcelain fingers were smooth and unblemished.

Leaning back into the plush leather chair, she exhaled a thin, elegant stream of smoke, regarding Tae-han with half-lidded, evaluating eyes.

"Does that mean you're content watching Executive Director Kang take the throne?"

Tae-han’s cunning eyes twitched with irritation. He was already on edge after one of his staunchest allies on the board of directors had vanished off the face of the earth. It took zero detective work to figure out whose handiwork that was. For a mere Executive Director to quietly erase a foundational board member of Haewon Group was sheer madness.

It was an execution that could only happen with Chairman Kang’s tacit blessing.

As rumors of Yoon's disappearance spread through the ranks, the remaining board members had begun to waver, and neutral shareholders were already murmuring that the Chairman’s favor had completely shifted to his second son.

Even so, what Sun-young was proposing crossed every rational boundary.

"Eliminating Jang Yi-an is suicide," Tae-han said flatly.

The kid was an international VIP—the direct grandson of a Triad kingpin whose late father had shared blood-brother ties with Chairman Kang. To put a hit on that boy and expect to walk away unscathed was pure delusion. Sun-young’s reckless greed almost made him laugh. He had anticipated some underhanded scheme when she called this meeting, but this was absurd.

"Who said anything about killing him?" she murmured through a haze of smoke. "A few shallow stab wounds will do the trick."

Raised by predatory loan sharks, Kim Sun-young was a far cry from a refined, delicate lady of high society.

"That will only blow back on us," Tae-han countered.

"The blowback won't hit us—it will fall entirely on Kang Il-hyun," she said, leaning forward. "If the Hong Kong heir bleeds under his roof, not even your father will be able to shield him."

Chairman Kang’s insistence on grooming Il-hyun despite board resistance was heavily anchored in his close syndicate ties with Hong Kong. The Triad bosses vastly preferred dealing with the ruthless, lethal Il-hyun over the bureaucratic Tae-han. Jang Yi-an’s visit was never just a friendly social call; it was a diplomatic inspection.

"It's too reckless," Tae-han warned, shaking his head. "If a single thing goes sideways... do you really think you can handle Il-hyun's retaliation?"

Sun-young ground her cigarette out in the crystal ashtray, bracing both forearms on the table as she leaned in close.

"Then how about this?"

"..."

"What if we take out Kang Il-hyun directly?"

Tae-han’s eyebrow shot up in disbelief. Is she insane?

"I protect my son," Sun-young whispered, her voice dropping into a venomous hiss, "and you secure your rightful succession."

He could see where her desperation was coming from. Unlike Tae-han, who merely viewed the delinquent Seok-joo as a useless nuisance, Il-hyun looked like a man who was actively waiting for an excuse to slaughter the kid. The violence was escalating rapidly—yesterday it was an ice pick to the skull; next time, it would be a severed head. Sun-young had finally realized that Il-hyun wasn't making empty threats.

"Have you forgotten who Kang Il-hyun is?" Tae-han sneered. "That demon would crawl his way back out of the depths of hell just to slit our throats."

"Which is why we take the clean route."

Tae-han fished out a cigarette, but his fingers trembled slightly, unable to bring himself to spark the flame. If this move failed, it was a one-way ticket to a shallow grave.

"If something goes wrong—"

"It won't."

"How can you be so certain?"

"Because," Sun-young smiled, a triumphant, wicked gleam lighting up her eyes, "I've already contracted the finest specialist in the industry."

Watching that smug, absolute confidence, Tae-han bit hard on the filter of his unlit smoke before snapping the tobacco cylinder in half and tossing it aside.

He picked up the photo of Jang Yi-an once more, studying the youth's face. Twenty-one years old. Still practically a child.

Tae-han's mental calculator clicked into overdrive. Waiting around passively was guaranteed defeat; taking a calculated gamble to sever Il-hyun’s limbs before the inauguration had its merits. All he had to do was play along on the surface. If the operation succeeded, Il-hyun was gone. If it went south, he could dump the entire blame onto Kim Sun-young and walk away clean.

"I suppose that makes us partners now, doesn't it?" Sun-young purred, extending a manicured hand across the table.

Tae-han hesitated for a heartbeat, set the photograph down, and took her hand in a firm grip.

"Indeed. Partners."

A faint tremor of anxiety still lingered in his gut, but the vivid mental image of Kang Il-hyun being cast aside, ruined and bleeding in the dirt, dissolved the fear instantly—replacing it with a surge of intoxicating, twisted euphoria.
